newsitem.title: USA: SEC bars broker on derivatives sales to Ohio towns.
newsitem.headline: SEC bars broker on derivatives sales to Ohio towns.

text.p: An SEC administrative law judge barred a former Hart Securities, Inc broker from the securities business for lying to 13 Ohio localities and school districts about $39 million in derivatives he sold them, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Friday.
Kenneth Schulte already was convicted in February 1997 on criminal convictions of wire, mail and securities fraud, SEC said in a press statement.
SEC said Schulte from 1990 and 1994 made "material misrepresentations and omissions" when selling over $39 million of derivative securities to at least 13 municipalities and school districts in Ohio.

The investors lost a total of $8.2 million in the deals, SEC said, adding Schulte also worked at Murchison Investment Bankers, Inc and Comprehensive Capital Corporation during the time of the alleged violations.
"Schulte was a willing and knowing participant in a very successful scheme to defraud small public entities with financially unsophisticated investing officials," the ALJ found, said SEC.
